rv.q: Micah Schraft’s “A Dog’s House” is a thought-provoking, darkly engaging play.
It's a discomfiting play, but under Kelleher's hand, it's mostly an absorbing experience, even if you can see what the inevitable outcome will be.
There’s still plenty to enjoy for anyone seeking some raw emotion.
This is certainly worth seeing and supporting.

cn.t: This bold, challenging drama about moral ambiguity after a dog kills a neighbor's pet earns praise for its sure-handed examination of difficult questions, though the emotionally gut-punching production is deemed impressive but flawed.
